unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 11-LEVEL: B1.3 THEME 4: FAMILY LIFE & HOME

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will create a project titled ''Family Dynamics and Shared Living Spaces'' exploring the progress of family life and its challenges across time and cultures. They will begin by describing the daily routines of their family members, comparing these to those of previous generations to show how roles and responsibilities have changed, using sentences like: ''Parents had taken full responsibility for chores before children started helping''. Next, they will focus on family traditions, hobbies, and interests, such as favourite sports or films, explaining how these activities strengthen relationships and allow for personal expression. Finally, students will research different types of families around the world, comparing them to their own experiences and reflecting on how cultural differences shape family life and shared living spaces. The project should include creative elements, such as interviews, photos, drawings, or videos, and will be presented in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''family life and home with its components such as family traditions, values, and customs (watching films together, preferences for films, music, and sports); family problems related to sharing a house and solutions'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student of an upper secondary school in year 11 may know what family traditions, values, and customs (watching films together, preferences for films, music, and sports); family problems related to sharing a house and solutions mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students of an upper secondary school in year 11, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''family life and home'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''sibling, great- grandmother/father, mother/father/brother/sister/daughter /son-in-law, spouse, half-sister/brother, distant relatives'' and also some structures such as ''My sisters were very hardworking; they prepared meals, tidied up, and set the table every day. Did your sibling like watching science fiction films as a teenager? My sister could ride a horse exceptionally well when she was younger. When I was a child, we used to live in a small cottage in the mountains.'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''family traditions, values, and customs (watching films together, preferences for films, music, and sports); family problems related to sharing a house and solutions'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To analyse family traditions, explore cultural variations, and debate the impact of modern technology on family practices in English through speaking and critical thinking skills by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Exploring Family Traditions and Modern Influences The teacher divides the class into groups of 4-5 students and assigns each group a specific family tradition or custom (e.g., celebrating birthdays, watching movies together, or having family meals) to research and present. Each group prepares a brief presentation that discusses the significance of the tradition in fostering family connections, provides examples of how different cultures celebrate similar traditions, and highlights potential challenges or conflicts associated with maintaining these practices. Then, groups debate whether modern technology (e.g., streaming services, online gaming) strengthens or weakens family traditions, using target vocabulary such as ''streaming service'', ''spoiler'', ''reunite'', ''to celebrate'', ''entertaining'', and ''to prepare''. In the end, the teacher provides constructive feedback on the presentations and debates, focusing on content and use of vocabulary. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To recognise family traditions, values, and customs in English by using target vocabulary. Activity: Match the Moments The teacher creates a matching activity where students match pictures with family-related vocabulary and concepts. For example, one column shows pictures such as a family celebrating a birthday, a messy room, a family watching TV, or someone setting a table, while the other column includes words or phrases like ''celebrating birthdays'', ''mess'', ''family meals'', and ''streaming service''. Students match the pictures with the correct word by drawing lines. After completing the activity, the teacher checks the answers as a class, discusses the significance of each image, and provides feedback on students’ understanding, pronunciation, and participation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
